title: Adaptive page-anchoring and temporal reclamation for paged-attention residency
creator: Priya Sethi
description:
Problem:
Paged attention currently suffers from suboptimal residency decisions that increase fragmentation and cause hotspots during bursty traffic. Existing heuristics evict based on LRU-like windows which miss short-lived temporal locality in multi-tenant workloads and result in wasted recompute or cold-KV fetches. Additionally, kernel selection for short/long-context work is not aware of page anchoring constraints, causing decode stalls during kernel handoffs.

Proposal summary:
Introduce an "adaptive page-anchor" residency mechanism plus a lightweight "temporal reclamation" scheduler that together optimize allocation and eviction for paged-attention KV storage. The system will: (1) assign anchors to pages representing stable prefix regions, (2) score page residency using a temporal locality window and affinity to active decode waves, and (3) perform reclamation in coordinated micro-batches that align with kernel handoff points to avoid decode stalls.

Design details:
- Page Anchors: when a prefill or decode references contiguous token ranges repeatedly within a short period, we mark the containing pages with a soft anchor tag and an anchor epoch. Anchored pages receive conservative eviction weight and are considered hot for kernel co-placement. Anchors decay exponentially if not re-referenced.
- Temporal Locality Score: each page maintains three inexpensive counters exposed as a small atomic struct: recent_hits (sliding window), last_touch_ts (for recency), and affinity_score (aggregated per decode wave id). The TTL of recent_hits adapts based on observed request inter-arrival distributions per tenant.
- Micro-reclamation scheduling: rather than global scans, reclamation runs as short jobs that pick candidate pages by lowest score but avoid evicting pages that are currently anchored or have affinity to an in-flight decode wave. Jobs align to kernel boundaries (e.g., between tiled attention kernels) so that eviction does not preempt an ongoing kernel that expects a resident page.
- Kernel-aware routing: add a small hint to the runtime router that preferences scheduling decode work onto GPU contexts where high-affinity anchored pages are resident; fallback policies remain unchanged. Kernel selection logic will prefer kernels with lower memory churn when several anchored pages are present.
- Fragment stitching and reuse: when eviction splits a previously contiguous fragment, we record fragment metadata to allow reclamation to preferentially reuse pieces that can be coalesced without heavy compaction.

Metrics and targets:
- 95th percentile decode latency reduction: target 6-10% on mixed short/long workloads.
- Cache fetch rate (MB/s from host): reduce by 10% in steady-state.
- Eviction-induced recompute events: reduce by 20% vs current baseline in staged workload.
- Overhead: per-request CPU cost budget <= 0.7% extra cycles on scheduler path.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Aggressive anchoring reduces churn but can increase memory pressure; anchoring thresholds must be tuned per-tenant or per-priority class.
- Kernel-aware routing improves tail latency but could increase cross-GPU affinity skew; we will guard with capacity-aware fallback.
- Recording fragment metadata increases metadata footprint; we will compress entries and TTL them aggressively.

Experiment plan:
1) Implement anchor tagging and temporal counters behind a runtime flag. 2) Run microbench on canary cluster with synthetic multi-tenant traffic (short convo bursts + occasional long context). 3) Measure metrics above and compare against baseline. 4) Enable micro-reclamation scheduler in staging and evaluate interplay with autoscaler. 5) Gradual rollout to 5% of production with telemetry dashboard and kill-switch.

Rollout and observability:
- New telemetry: page_anchor_state, temporal_score, reclamation_job_latency, kernel_affinity_misses.
- Dashboards: per-tenant residency heatmap, eviction/recompute events, tail latency by model-size.
- Rollout: feature flag -> staging -> 5% prod -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if recompute events spike > 2x baseline.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: anchor heuristics tuned poorly for bursty real customers. Mitigation: provide per-tenant defaults and runtime tuning knobs surfaced in Console.
- Risk: scheduler misalignment with kernels causes short stalls. Mitigation: integrate eviction jobs with kernel boundary signals and include a conservative grace window initially.

Deliverables:
- Runtime change: anchor metadata, temporal counters, micro-reclaimer.
- Router change: kernel-aware affinity hinting.
- Telemetry and dashboards.
- Bench harness and regression tests.

Estimated effort: 8 points across 3 sprints (design + implementation + tuning).
